question: Do fixed missense-predictor ensembles distinguish variants that were pure VUS in historical ClinVar releases but were independently resolved by the 2026-08 release?
historical_test_eligibility: ProteinGym clinical missense SNV with all five component scores and an existing frozen family-held-out out-of-fold prediction
historical aggregate germline classification is Uncertain significance
historical submission-level records include at least one VUS and no Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic or Benign/Likely benign submission
current 2026-08 aggregate classification is one-sided Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic or Benign/Likely benign
current submission-level records contain no opposing pathogenic-versus-benign classification
current ProteinGym binary label agrees with the 2026-08 resolved side

primary_high_confidence: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts
truth_tiers.secondary_all_resolved: all nonconflicting resolved P/LP or B/LB aggregate classifications

primary_models.frozen_existing_ensemble: family-held-out fixed_prob from the completed global30 ProteinGym experiment
primary_models.frozen_existing_comparator: family-held-out PoET base_prob from the same completed experiment
primary_models.temporal_clean_recipe: weighted5_p1 using PoET, TranceptEVE_L, GEMME, EVE, and ESM1b; score orientation, performance weights and one-dimensional calibration estimated only from variants already resolved at the historical cutoff
primary_models.temporal_clean_comparator: PoET calibrated using only variants already resolved at the historical cutoff

uncertainty_unit: MMseqs global30 homology component, resampled with replacement
minimum_success_criteria: at least 100 primary high-confidence resolved historical VUS in the primary cutoff, preferably 200
ensemble improves at least one proper scoring rule with a cluster-bootstrap confidence interval above zero and does not worsen the other proper scoring rule
AUROC difference confidence interval above zero or clear proper-score superiority
same directional result in at least two historical cutoffs
direction retained in the high-confidence truth tier
direction retained after excluding current submission conflicts
failure_criteria: ensemble superiority disappears in historical VUS
effect disappears in the high-confidence truth tier
effect is driven by a small number of homology clusters
temporal-clean recipe fails even if the retrospective frozen prediction appears positive
forbidden_actions: retune ensemble architecture or thresholds using historical VUS outcomes
select a cutoff because it gives the strongest result
combine clinical and functional truth into one endpoint
claim novelty of temporal VUS validation without direct literature comparison
